text:
Navigate your code's history

with this week's productivity tip of the week in #vscode

00:00:00,040 --> 00:00:01,325 When you're working in a lot 00:00:01,325 --> 00:00:02,309 of files, it's easy 00:00:02,356 --> 00:00:03,160 to lose your way. 00:00:03,400 --> 00:00:04,691 Luckily VS Code has built-in 00:00:04,691 --> 00:00:06,600 navigation history to help. 00:00:09,320 --> 00:00:10,377 If you want to navigate 00:00:10,377 --> 00:00:11,434 back to where you were, 00:00:11,479 --> 00:00:13,100 you can use Alt + left arrow 00:00:13,100 --> 00:00:14,362 to go back, and you can do the 00:00:14,416 --> 00:00:15,148 opposite to navigate 00:00:15,148 --> 00:00:17,119 forward with Alt + right arrow. 00:00:17,280 --> 00:00:18,400 If you want to navigate your 00:00:18,400 --> 00:00:19,935 entire history, you can use 00:00:19,935 --> 00:00:21,408 CTRL + Tab to tab through 00:00:21,464 --> 00:00:22,599 your editor history. 00:00:22,760 --> 00:00:24,640 Now I'm on a Windows machine, so I'm 00:00:24,640 --> 00:00:26,160 showing you the Windows shortcuts. 00:00:26,240 --> 00:00:27,271 You can always look these up 00:00:27,271 --> 00:00:29,575 by running the Open Keyboard Shortcuts command, 00:00:29,674 --> 00:00:31,253 and if I search for "go back", 00:00:31,370 --> 00:00:32,287 then we can see that it's 00:00:32,287 --> 00:00:33,707 showing Alt + left arrow key. 00:00:33,707 --> 00:00:34,520 And you can easily change 00:00:34,520 --> 00:00:36,156 these key bindings by clicking 00:00:36,156 --> 00:00:37,410 the pencil icon to edit 00:00:37,450 --> 00:00:38,720 and then using the keys that you 00:00:38,780 --> 00:00:40,766 want as the shortcut and press enter.

plan.title: Navigate your code's history
plan.summary: VS Code keeps a navigation history you can retrace with Alt+Left/Right and Ctrl+Tab, and you can find or rebind those shortcuts in Keyboard Shortcuts.

moves.title: Jump back with Alt+Left, forward with Alt+Right
moves.intent: Use Alt+Left arrow to return to your previous cursor location in VS Code, and Alt+Right arrow to go forward again.
moves.evidence: you can use Alt + left arrow

moves.title: Tab through your whole editor history with Ctrl+Tab
moves.intent: Hold Ctrl+Tab in VS Code to cycle through every file in your editor history instead of just stepping one back or forward.

moves.title: Look up any shortcut in Keyboard Shortcuts
moves.intent: Run the Open Keyboard Shortcuts command and search (e.g. "go back") to see exactly which keys a VS Code command is bound to.
moves.evidence: by running the Open Keyboard Shortcuts command,

moves.title: Rebind a shortcut to keys you prefer
moves.intent: In Keyboard Shortcuts, click the pencil icon on a command, press the new key combination, and hit enter to change its binding.
